solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tea at start of day here in Africa

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
opening letter of day

explanation.surface: A visitor notes that tea is taken first thing in the morning in some African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here in Africa' points to a country on that continent, defined by place rather than by a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked country in north-central Africa, so it is a place on that continent.

clue.text: Persist in opposing money European Union raised

indicators.note: in a down answer, raised means lifted upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
tin is old slang for money
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone keeps on fighting against money from the European Union being increased.
explanation.definitionFit: To continue is to carry on without stopping, which is what persisting means.

clue.text: Specialised language upcoming artist understood

indicators.note: in a down answer, upcoming means coming up the column, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
to have got something is to have understood it

explanation.surface: A promising new artist was understood only through technical jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the jargon or slang of a particular group, a vocabulary used by insiders.

clue.text: Uninformed tirade after soldier returns with refusal

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the word for soldier is read backwards
after places the tirade at the end, behind the other pieces

blocks.note: GI is an American soldier
a refusal is a no
a tirade is a rant

explanation.surface: A soldier comes home, refuses something and launches into an ill-informed rant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ignorant lacks knowledge, which is exactly being uninformed; both adjectives describe a person without facts.

clue.text: US vice-president once nursing small shrub

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the name wraps around the letter for small

blocks.note: Al Gore was vice-president under Bill Clinton
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A former US vice-president is tending a small bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered evergreen bush common on heathland, also called furze or whin.

clue.text: Upfront ambassador to oppose such a sale system

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing the system, not the system itself

blocks.note: overt means open, done upfront
HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
to counter is to oppose

explanation.surface: An outspoken ambassador objects to a particular way of selling things.
explanation.walkthrough: HE for an ambassador is a crossword convention from the honorific His Excellency.
explanation.definitionFit: Over-the-counter trading sells goods or shares directly rather than through prescription or an exchange, a description of the system.

clue.text: Distinctive quality, trait, unusual – objection by English follows

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of the trait are put out of their normal order
follows puts the objection and English after the rearranged letters

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A list describing a distinctive quality, an unusual trait, then an English objection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trait' looks like part of the definition, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An attribute is a characteristic feature belonging to someone or something, a quality that marks it out.

clue.text: Actor John to become relaxed

blocks.note: first meaning: John ..., the English actor who played Inspector Morse
second meaning: to melt or soften, of a person growing less stiff

explanation.surface: An actor called John is told to loosen up.
explanation.walkthrough: John Thaw starred as Inspector Morse in the British TV detective series.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice that thaws softens, and a person who thaws becomes friendlier and less tense, losing their reserve.

clue.text: Sit-in ritual with aim to change doctrine

indicators.note: to change the letters is to alter their arrangement into something new

blocks.note: the three words sit-in, ritual and aim, every letter used; with only joins them

explanation.surface: Protesters stage a routine sit-in intended to alter an official policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Utilitarianism is the ethical theory that the right act brings the greatest happiness to the greatest number, a philosophical creed.

clue.text: Non-conformists begin to depart spa town at first travelling South

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so just that one is used
at first again keeps only the first letter of the following word

blocks.note: first letter of depart
Evian-les-Bains is a French spa town famous for bottled water
first letter of travelling
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Rebels start to leave a spa resort, first heading south.
explanation.definitionFit: Deviants depart from accepted norms of behaviour, which is what non-conformists do.

clue.text: Close, be quick to embrace wife as this brings bed to mind?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so one word wraps round the letter for wife

blocks.note: nigh means near or close
to tear is to rush along quickly
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to hurry and hug their wife, the scene making them think of going to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint rather than a synonym: pyjamas and nighties make you think of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas and nightdresses are clothing worn in bed, so seeing them naturally calls sleep and bedtime to mind.

clue.text: More involved in next race

indicators.note: something involved in a phrase is caught up inside it, so the letters sit within these words

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Extra runners have been entered for the following race.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra and more are synonyms, both meaning additional, as in extra time or more time.

clue.text: Guys having cultivated learning – elitist? Not right!

definitions.note: a plural noun for a collective noun: the answer is the group of such people

indicators.note: cultivated ground is worked over and turned, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
not right tells the solver to leave out the abbreviation for right

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: People who have acquired cultivated learning are accused of elitism, and the speaker says that is unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one long description of clever people, but 'cultivated' is the signal; R comes out of learning before the letters are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: The intelligentsia is the educated class of a society, the thinkers and scholars, so it covers such guys collectively.

clue.text: Leading group unexpectedly beaten?

blocks.note: a side that is up is ahead or leading
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A sports report wonders whether the team in the lead was surprisingly defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a sporting sense: a favourite that is upset loses unexpectedly.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport an upset is a surprise defeat of the favourite, so a team upset has been beaten against expectations.

clue.text: Newcomer shelters ultimately evil killer

indicators.note: to shelter is to cover and protect, so the newcomer word goes round the other letter
ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: a stranger is someone newly arrived
last letter of evil

explanation.surface: A new arrival in town harbours a wicked murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler kills by throttling, so the word names a particular kind of murderer.

clue.text: Like mother-of-pearl source sadly not available to begin with

indicators.note: something going sadly is going badly wrong, so the letters fall out of their order
to begin with puts the abbreviation for not available at the front

blocks.note: NA is the usual abbreviation for not available
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A jeweller laments that the supply of mother-of-pearl is unavailable at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is the technical name for mother-of-pearl, and nacreous is its adjective, describing that iridescent shell lining.

clue.text: Till sacked, she's endlessly messing about

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter of the pronoun is dropped
messing about means fooling around in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A shop worker sacked from the till is always fooling around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Till' looks like a verb or 'until'; it is the cash register. The 's after she is read as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A till is a cash register, and a cash desk is the counter where payment is taken, so they are equivalent.

clue.text: Seek to impress. Learn, turning to Lear perhaps?

blocks.note: surface reading: studying a King Lear text, or learning to become like Lear
setter's reading: the word learn loses its final letter N and becomes Lear, a name, by dropping that letter

explanation.surface: A student studies Shakespeare in the hope of impressing people.
explanation.walkthrough: N is an abbreviation for name; drop it from learn and you get Lear, so the second half is a playful picture of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To name-drop is to mention famous acquaintances casually, a showy attempt to impress others.

clue.text: Supports for Members?

blocks.note: surface reading: backing given to members of a club or parliament
setter's reading: members are limbs, and these support the upper limbs on a chair

explanation.walkthrough: The capital M suggests Members of Parliament; members here are body parts, the arms resting on a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Members can mean limbs, and the padded side pieces of a chair hold up a sitter's forearms, supporting those limbs.

clue.text: End of series, old, very good

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
mega is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A viewer judges the final episode of an old series as brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so it stands for the final item of any sequence.

clue.text: Interest maybe of mine under ocean, mysterious

indicators.note: something mysterious is obscure and puzzling, so the letters are jumbled out of plain view

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Someone takes a curious interest in a strange mine beneath the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' looks like curiosity; it is money earned on savings, one example of the answer, hence 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unearned income is money from investments rather than work, and interest on savings is a typical example of it.

clue.text: Currently popular but without hope of success

blocks.note: first meaning: ..., read as two words, fashionable at present
second meaning: a situation where every option leads to losing

explanation.surface: Something fashionable at the moment is nevertheless doomed to fail.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-win situation offers no chance of a good outcome, while now in splits to mean in fashion right now.

clue.text: Nightclub security man uncovered small portion

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer layer, so the first and last letters are removed

blocks.note: a bouncer guards the door of a club

explanation.surface: A club doorman is exposed as having pocketed a little share.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small unit of weight, so figuratively a tiny amount, as in not an ounce of sense.

clue.text: Very large plot to exclude outsiders in City

indicators.note: excluding the outsiders of a word removes its outer letters, leaving the middle

blocks.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for very large
the inner letters of plot

explanation.surface: A huge piece of land keeps strangers out of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway, so it is a city, defined only by its category.

clue.text: Conductor reversing some exit losses

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of them is used, the run of letters inside
reversing means going backwards, so that run of letters is read from right to left

blocks.note: letters inside the two words, taken before turning round

explanation.surface: A bus or train conductor is turning back some losses at the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests a ticket collector; it is Georg Solti, the Hungarian-British orchestral conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Georg Solti was a celebrated orchestral and opera conductor, long music director of the Chicago Symphony Orchestra.

clue.text: One from San Francisco, say, our group finds more demanding

blocks.note: we is our group, the speakers themselves
sterner means stricter, more exacting

explanation.surface: A visitor from San Francisco finds our team a harder taskmaster than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: San Francisco is on the US west coast, so a native of it is a person from the West, given by example.

clue.text: Working staff in debt awaiting court's decision?

indicators.note: in places the word for staff inside the colour that means owing money

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
to be in the red is to be in debt
to man is to staff, as in man the desk

explanation.surface: Employees working while in debt wait to hear what the court decides about them.
explanation.walkthrough: Being on remand means held in custody, or on bail, before trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner on remand is held pending trial, so they are waiting for a court to rule on their case.

clue.text: Leading elements of dissertation, extremely esoteric paper, hard to follow

indicators.note: the leading elements of words are their first letters, so each word gives only its opening one

blocks.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A thesis is criticised as an extremely obscure paper that is hard to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep argument is profound and complex, so it is difficult for an ordinary reader to understand.
